title: Operator Runbooks: Compact Playbook and Knowledge Transfer
author: Luca Reyes
body:
Overview

This compact playbook captures the essential operator runbooks, decision matrices, and knowledge-transfer activities needed for safe handoffs across platform teams (Serving Runtime, Platform, SRE, and Customer Ops). It is intended for: new operators, oncall rotation transfers, and cross-team runbook synthesis prior to major rollouts.

Why this exists

- Reduce mean time to mitigation (MTTM) by providing concise, actionable steps for common LLM inference platform failure modes.
- Standardize alert-to-action mappings so operators take consistent, safe steps.
- Ensure knowledge captured in a compact format that can be embedded in oncall bundles and runbook cards.

Quick links

- Primary dashboard: Platform Operator Compact — Grafana (dash id: platform-operator-compact)
- Oncall playbook hub: /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks
- Incident channel prefix: #platform-ops
- Pager policy: Escalate after 12 minutes if L2 not ACKed

Runbook structure (template)

Each runbook card should use this compact structure so operators can scan quickly:

1) Symptom summary (1 sentence)
2) Impact (SLO/SLA buckets)
3) Immediate mitigations (ordered list)
4) Triage commands / queries (promql, kubectl, mysql, redis)
5) Owner and escalations (roles + slack tags)
6) Recovery and rollback steps
7) Post-incident actions (checklist for retrospectives)

Example: Prefix-Cache Degradation (compact)

- Symptom: Elevated prefix-cache miss rate > 5% for > 3m and token latency p95 > 250ms.
- Impact: Token latency SLO (foreground) breached if sustained > 5m. Estimated customer impact: high for interactive chat tenants.
- Immediate mitigations:
  1. Toggle emergency local-serving-mode: curl -XPOST https://ops-api/internal/v1/pools/cache-prefetch?action=emergency-warmup
  2. Promote read-only cache snapshot from fallback region: opsctl cache promote --region=eu-west-1 --pool=prefix-cache-pool-1
  3. If above fails, enable routing fallthrough to smaller model variant (see gating policy).
- Triage queries (promql):
  - prefix_cache_miss_ratio{pool="prefix-cache-pool-1"} > 0.05 for 3m
  - runtime_token_latency_seconds_bucket{quantile="0.95"}
- Owners: platform-operator-oncall (@platform-ops), runtime-kernel-owner (@runtime-team)
- Recovery: allow cache to stabilize for 15m, then run integrity-check: opsctl cache verify --pool=prefix-cache-pool-1
- Post-incident: file retro using the compact retro template (section below).

Decision matrix: when to failover vs degrade

This matrix helps choose between graceful degradation, regional failover, model variant fallback, and hard failover. Each row is scored 0..5 across: customer-impact, recovery-confidence, cost-delta, and compliance-risk.

| Condition | Recommended action | Min score to auto-execute | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Minor latency spike (p95 < 300ms, <5% tenants affected) | Activate adaptive-batching and do not failover | 9 | Non-disruptive; preferred default |
| KV cache partial corruption (confirmed) | Promote read-only snapshot, canary warmup region | 12 | Requires operator confirmation if compliance-sensitive |
| Sustained model OOMs across >2 nodes | Trigger model-variant fallback | 14 | Fallback must preserve API contract; inform customers |
| Control-plane outage in region | Regional traffic rehome to secondary region | 18 | Requires network & infra coordination |

Alert routing and actionable thresholds

- Alert categories:
  - SEV-1: Hard availability loss (api-availability < 99.5% for 5m). Pager to primary oncall and EM.
  - SEV-2: Resource saturation risk (GPU mem pressure > 90% on 3+ nodes for 5m). Pager to ops team.
  - SEV-3: Performance degradation (foreground p95 token latency > 300ms for 10m). Notify oncall only.

Standard alert definition examples (Prometheus-style)

1) SEV-1 API availability
  ALERT ApiAvailabilityLow
  IF sum(rate(api_request_errors_total[5m])) / sum(rate(api_request_total[5m])) > 0.005
  FOR 5m
  LABELS { severity="sev1" }
  ANNOTATIONS { summary="API error rate >0.5%" }

2) SEV-2 GPU mem pressure
  ALERT GpuMemoryPressure
  IF avg_over_time(gpu_memory_utilization[5m]) > 0.90
  FOR 5m
  LABELS { severity="sev2" }
  ANNOTATIONS { summary="Average GPU memory >90%" }

Dashboard guidance (what to show)

Every compact dashboard should contain a single row with these panels:
- API availability (last 15m/1h/24h)
- Token latency histogram (p50/p90/p95/p99) broken down by tenant-criticality
- Resource heatmap: GPU mem, GPU util, CPU steal, network egress
- Cache health: miss ratio, fill rate, snapshot lag
- Routing topology: active model variant counts and rehome events

Runbook cards and embedding in bundles

- Each runbook card must include a 1-line TL;DR, a 3-step immediate action list, and 2 validated triage queries.
- Cards live in the oncall bundle (S3 archive) and are attached to Slack alerts by the Alert Router. See attachment schema: {runbook_id, version, digest}.

Handoff checklist (operator knowledge transfer)

1) Pre-handoff (24–48h before shift change):
   - Share active incidents and mitigation status.
   - Confirm no ongoing canaries or feature gates.
   - Verify local dashboards show green for your buckets.
2) Handoff moment (synchronous or async):
   - Run the runbook self-check (see checklist below).
   - Broadcast to #platform-ops: "handoff from <A> to <B> — no active incidents" or list active mitigations.
3) Post-handoff (within 2h):
   - Recipient runs a quick smoke test: 3 sample API calls for foreground and background paths, validate token latency and embedding success.

Runbook self-check (operator)

- Verify Alert policy ACK window is set to 6m and long-running alerts pinned.
- Confirm access: kubectl, opsctl, alert-router, and S3-runbook-bucket keys valid.
- Ensure runbook card version matches dashboard digest.

Retrospective compact template (for fast capture)

1) Summary (2 sentences)
2) Timeline (key events with timestamps)
3) Root cause hypothesis (one line)
4) What worked / what didn’t (bullets)
5) Action items (owner + target date)

Sample retro entry for the prefix-cache case above:

- Summary: Cache snapshot promotion did not complete due to transient S3 permission denial; operators failed to promote using fallback.
- Timeline: 2026-07-12 11:03 alert -> 11:10 mitigation attempted -> 11:25 fallback triggered -> 11:50 degraded mode restored
- Root cause: IAM role mis-attachment during a recent key rotation.
- Action items: (1) Rollback key-rotation procedure (owner: infra-tooling, due: 2026-07-25), (2) Add IAM validation step to runbook (owner: platform, due: 2026-07-28)

Roadmap tie-ins and ownership

Short term (next 90 days)
- Deliver compact runbook index (searchable by symptom and owner). Owner: platform-runbook-ops. Target: 2026-09-01.
- Add runbook card attachments to the Alert Router with automatic version checks. Owner: alerting-frontend. Target: 2026-10-01.

Medium term (3–9 months)
- Integrate runbook cards into the operator certification curriculum and gamified oncall drills. Owner: training-team. Target: 2027-01-15.
- Build a guided remediation UI for common mitigations (e.g., cache promote, model rollback). Owner: runtime-ui. Target: 2027-03-01.

Long term (9–18 months)
- Automate low-risk mitigations with policy gates (canary first, manual approve on metric change). Owner: autonoma-ops. Target: 2027-Q4.

Appendix: Useful commands and snippets

- Cache promote (example):
  opsctl cache promote --pool=prefix-cache-pool-1 --from=eu-west-1 --to=us-west-2 --dry-run=false
- Verify GPU memory pressure (kubectl):
  kubectl top pods --namespace=runtime | grep gpu | sort -k3 -nr | head -n 20
- Promql examples: token latency p95 by tenant tier:
  histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(token_latency_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, tenant_tier))

Contacts and escalation tags

- Primary oncall: @platform-ops (rotates daily)
- Runtime kernel owner: @runtime-team
- Capacity & GPU fleet: @gpu-fleet-response
- Security (for suspected compromise): @security-incident

Notes and maintenance

- This compact playbook is intended to be opinionated and minimal. For full-length investigations and artefacts, link to the relevant runbook in /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks and the detailed postmortem in /confluence/eng-platform/retrospectives.
- Ownership: Luca Reyes (author) — please escalate changes via the runbook PR process: create PR in docs-runbooks repo and add reviewers: Maya Chen, Arjun Iyer.

End of document
